Select the Pen tool (P) and draw a straight two-point line, clicking at roughly (200,300) and (500,300). Do NOT press Enter — pressing Enter is "Done" and ends the vector edit session. Staying in the vector edit session, click directly on the middle of the existing segment at about (350,300) to insert one extra anchor point onto the path itself (a single continuous vertex, not a new path). If the pen is still extending the chain, switch to the node/path edit affordance first so that a click on the segment inserts a point rather than starting a new path.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

With the Pen tool (P), inside ONE vector edit session draw two separate open strokes: draw the first stroke, then press Escape (NOT Enter) to finish that chain while staying in the same vector edit session (pressing Enter is "Done" and exits the session, which would make the second stroke a separate object). Draw the second stroke as another subpath of the same vector. Then pen-click a loose endpoint of one stroke and click the loose endpoint of the other so a connecting segment joins them into a single continuous path. Exit the session when done.

Note: for open paths export_svg emits one "M" command per segment, so seeing multiple "M" subpaths in the SVG is normal serialization — it does NOT mean the strokes are disconnected. Judge success by whether the two strokes are joined into one connected path (one connected component with two loose ends).
